docs.title: Core Rules
docs.html:
The SHZ-TTRPG is traditionally designed to be played with a d20. The GM may use different dice to add color to various actions, but the system is built on the d20.

DEATH

In the game, death occurs when the player dies as a result of RP. In this regard, the GM may, at their initiative, end with the player's death based on the status of the limbs and the rolls made in the last action.

DEATH SAVE THROW

When the character faces death, it serves as a last resort for the player, if available. GMs are advised to turn this system off entirely for players seeking a challenge.

Each player has the right to make 1 death save throw, which can be reset only by spending inspiration points (after each reset, the inspiration points required increase by 1).

The death save throw works similarly to DnD. The player rolls a d6. On a 1-2-3, one mark goes in the death box; on a 4-5-6, one mark goes in the save box. Whichever reaches 3 first happens. Death: the character dies. Save: the character survives as critically wounded.

LEVELING

After each level gained in the game, you earn an Ability Point that can be used to open an ability tree, unlock an ability or raise an ability's level. The player starts the game at level 0 with 1 ability point and 1 open expertise tree

The level cap per campaign is 10; in long or connected campaigns the GM can raise this cap up to 15. To take the 3rd level of an ability, the character's level must be at least 4. When a tree's stat reaches 10, the guaranteed point that would go to that stat on leveling up is given to another stat of the player's choice.

ABILITY TREES

Each expertise tree has 8 abilities: 1 root ability, branches A and B (3 abilities each), each ending with its own finisher ability, and 1 sub-branch ability that splits off from the first ability of a branch. The BRANCH field in the ability files shows the ability's position (Root, A, A′, B, B′).

  • First ability of a branch: Requires at most 3 in the main stat.
  • Middle ability: Requires 4–5 in the main stat and one secondary stat; its predecessor is the branch's first ability.
  • Sub-branch: Requires 5 in the main stat and one secondary stat; its predecessor is the ability it splits off from.
  • Finisher: Requires 7 in the main stat, 4–5 in a secondary stat and a character level of at least 6–7; its predecessor is the branch's middle ability.
  • Synergy (Chemistry): Some abilities gain an extra effect when taken together with a specific ability from another branch or tree. These effects are written under the SYNERGY heading in the ability files.

STATS

Stats directly affect the action rolls you make. GMs who want to make the game harder are advised to manipulate the success thresholds through the story rather than changing the players' bonuses.

Formula: d20 + stat ≥ threshold.
Reference Threshold Table: { Very Easy 7 / Easy 9 / Medium 13 / Hard 15 / Very Hard 19 / Uber 22}
Nat20 and Nat1 are evaluated outside the table. They represent the best/worst possible outcome, respectively.

There is a minimum-0 rule for stats (except Klang). The maximum is 10.

To raise stats in the game, you must gain a "Level". On each level-up, 2+1 of the character's stats each get a 1 bonus (ability-based boosts are outside this rule): 1 stat is awarded based on the character's actions during the level, while the other 1 goes to the symbol stat of the player's expertise tree. The extra 1 stat goes to the MVP among all players leveling up. Since not every player has to level up at the same time within a session, these points can be distributed later. However, so that this point is not distributed too late, if a lagging player is 3 or more levels behind the level at which the MVP is awarded, they are excluded from the MVP calculation. Example: (Player A: lv3, B: lv6, C:lv7 the lv6 MVP is decided between B and C)

Leveling up is traditionally used at 1/2 per session, but this decision is ultimately left to the GM. The game has no built-in EXP system.

At the start of the game, players are given 2+2 stats (excluding the +2 Klang stat; everyone gets +2 Klang at the start). 2 points go to the attribute of the chosen starting expertise tree, while the other 2 stat points are left to the player to distribute among the stats other than the chosen expertise tree's attribute.

docs.title: Character
docs.html:
COSMETIC

1- Character Name

The name the character will use throughout the story. It does not directly affect RP, but it is best to choose a name that fits the chosen nationality.

2- Character Age

The character's age must be between 18 and 60. Old or Young characters are not suitable for the story (there may be exceptions for 60+.)

3- Character Alignment

Determines the character's general faction. Alignment is not decisive within RP, but setting it is necessary for the overall portrait.

4- Character Nationality

Due to the nature of the universe, the concepts of "Race" and "Nationality" can affect communication within RP.

5- Character's Money

Although it is generally not recommended to put it at the center of the story, "Reichsmark" can be used in the story.

6- Character Corruption Level

Every character has a Corruption level between 0 and 13. Corruption represents mental health. Corruption increases especially with the use of substances such as Amphetamine and Pervitin, which contains methamphetamine, used to relieve stress in combat.

7- Character Body Chart

The game has a body chart showing the health and mechanization status of all of a character's limbs. Wounds taken, applied bandages and installed attachments are tracked here.

8- Player's Inspiration Points

Given to players directly by the GM for good RP or as compensation for a GM error. One inspiration can be spent for a re-roll. More than one inspiration point can also be used for decisions that could be considered meta. If Inspiration drops below 0 (it can mostly be used by the GM as a penalty, or by GM-player agreement the player can even take Inspiration on credit. The final decision rests with the GM.), the player takes −2 on every roll for each point below zero.

FEATURES

HEALTH AND BODY : A character's health is not expressed as a number. The character's state of health is shown through the image in the game that represents the character's body. Augmentation is also managed in this area. Each character has 1 augment per limb slot.

In the game, every character has 4 separate features:

STATS

Stats are the attribute points used in in-game rolls and needed to unlock Abilities. Stat points are affected by Perks and in-game level-ups.

PERKS

Perks are chosen at the start of the game and affect the player's RP throughout the game. On the perk selection screen the player starts with + selection points and can take as many perks as they like as long as the total does not go negative. Any + selection points left over after perk selection are converted into stats. The system is as follows:

(Perk Points to Convert + 1) / 2, rounded down.

The starting Perk points are set by the GM; giving more can be used to make the game easier. The base recommended to GMs is +0 or +2.

ABILITIES

The game has abilities that can be used actively/passively. Abilities are gained at the start of the game and during play. Gaining abilities requires character level, and new abilities unlock at each level. Some abilities require a stat minimum.

In the game, every ability belongs to an expertise tree. Each character can have 2 expertise trees. You start the game with 1 expertise tree, and new trees are opened with ability points.

AUGMENTATION

Players may start the game with an augment. (This must be agreed with the GM. It is not integrated into the system, and starting the game with an augment is not recommended.) Augments can be fitted to any player entirely as a result of RP through the right systems. Augments may have their own abilities or stat modifiers.

docs.title: Body and Wounds
docs.html:
On the game sheet, each part is shown separately on a drawing of body anatomy. Table 2 serves this purpose. The first shows the health/bandage/equipment status of the player's body parts, the other shows the Augmentation fitted to that area.

LIMB DAMAGE STATES

Intact → Scratched → Lightly Wounded → Badly Wounded → Unusable → Severed

If a bandage gets dirty, it loses its effect, the wound applies a negative effect (formula below) and it moves to the Bandaged (Dirty) state.

EFFECTS:

APPLIES TO ACTION ROLLS IN WHICH THE LIMB IS USED:

INTACTNo Effect
BANDAGED (CLEAN)-Previous/2 → Round Down
BANDAGED (DIRTY)-Previous*3/4
SCRATCHED-1
LIGHTLY WOUNDED-2
BADLY WOUNDED-5
UNUSABLE-15
SEVERED-20

Rather than being systematized, the progression of wounds is left to the RP run by the GM. Wounds and their progression are deliberately not systematized, to leave room for creativity.

AUGMENTATION

The forms of Augmentation are generally left to the GM's imagination, but the core purpose of Augmentation is to offer players a second way out of the game's difficulty besides stats/abilities, and to diversify gameplay. GMs are especially advised to create Augment types that have their own unique features but cost stat points. Example Augmentations are in the "Augmentations" subfolder.

A player's ability to use Augmentation is measured by "Klang". Every player starts the game with +2 Klang. If Klang drops below zero, all rolls the player makes are penalized by that negative amount, and the augmented limb may break apart or malfunction during an action.

BODY PARTS

The human body consists of various parts, and the character's body is divided into parts with a right/left distinction.

The action effects of limb wounds are left to the GM's discretion. A scratch on the hand does not have to apply to every action that uses the hand, but the wound may open further (for example, catching something falling from above with the back of your hand).

docs.title: Corruption
docs.html:
Indicates how "Corrupted" the character is. It is shown on a 0-13 scale. It can be raised and lowered in various ways in the game (Addictions, Pervitin). The starting value is Corruption 0.

CORRUPTION STATUS TABLE

  1. 0No effect at all
  2. 1A ( + 2 ) roll effect applies to every black magic roll the player makes.
  3. 2No negative effect
  4. 3From this level on, the player gains +1 Klang for each point of Corruption.
  5. 4From this level on, the player gains +1 to black magic actions (esoteric abilities such as SHZ sigils) for each point of Corruption. (+2 at Corruption 5, +3 at 6, and so on)
  6. 5The "Cower" state unlocks. A trigger roll for Cower is made when you take damage from an enemy. If the player is in the "Cower" state, they cannot take actions until the state passes. To escape the Cower state, a "Sanita" roll must be made
  7. 6The "attack" actions of characters at this level become savage. They spill more blood and spend more resources.
  8. 7Corruption that reaches this level cannot be reduced below 7.
  9. 8The character's actions start to become unstable. Mechanics such as higher rolls to complete actions or nerve-control rolls may be imposed by the DM depending on the player's role.
  10. 9The "Frenzy" state unlocks. A trigger roll for Frenzy is made when you kill an enemy. If the player enters the "Frenzy" state, they attack another target in their line of sight. Frenzy can chain. (Frenzy attacks are strengthened at close range and weakened at long range.)
  11. 10From this level on, Pervitin / Methamphetamine no longer affects the player's Corruption level
  12. 11The character's actions become seriously unstable
  13. 12The character's actions become completely unstable.
  14. 13The character's mental health collapses. Death occurs.

PERVITIN / METHAMPHETAMINE

In the game, players can use Pervitin or similar products to escape situations such as acute stress. (Methamphetamine/amphetamine-based drug substances do not have to be presented to players by the GM only as Pervitin) When the substance is used, the character calms down and is freed from negative stress state effects, but must make a Corruption effect roll:

If Corruption Level < 10:

If d20 + Sanita − Corruption/3 ≥ threshold, Corruption does not increase
